data.content:
EcoToxFred here. I queried the graph for pairs of substances linked by JOINT_DRIVER_WITH and then checked whether those pairs are detected at the same sites (detection defined as median_concentration > 0 on MEASURED_AT).

Top co-driver pairs by frequency (examples from the top of the list)
- Methoxychlor — Terbutylazine: frequency 53
- Cyanuric acid — Indeno(1,2,3-cd)pyrene: frequency 48
- Endrin — Indeno(1,2,3-cd)pyrene: frequency 47
- Benzo(b)fluoranthene — Iomeprol: frequency 44
- Metazachlor — Carbofuran: frequency 44

Do these pairs tend to be detected at the same sites?
For the same top-frequency pairs, I computed site-level co-detection and overlap:
- Terbutylazine (sites 2846) and Methoxychlor (sites 17), both at 14 sites; Jaccard 0.0049
  - Conditional overlap: 82.4% of Methoxychlor sites also have Terbutylazine; 0.49% of Terbutylazine sites also have Methoxychlor
- Cyanuric acid (17) and Indeno(1,2,3-cd)pyrene (1144), both 17; Jaccard 0.0149
  - Conditional overlap: 100% of Cyanuric acid sites also have Indeno; 1.49% of Indeno sites also have Cyanuric acid
- Endrin (108) and Indeno(1,2,3-cd)pyrene (1144), both 79; Jaccard 0.0673
  - Conditional overlap: 73.2% of Endrin sites also have Indeno; 6.9% of Indeno sites also have Endrin
- Benzo(b)fluoranthene (1262) and Iomeprol (318), both 78; Jaccard 0.0519
  - Conditional overlap: 6.18% of Benzo(b) sites also have Iomeprol; 24.5% of Iomeprol sites also have Benzo(b)
- Metazachlor (2787) and Carbofuran (183), both 157; Jaccard 0.0558
  - Conditional overlap: 5.63% of Metazachlor sites also have Carbofuran; 85.8% of Carbofuran sites also have Metazachlor

Interpretation grounded in the data:
- Overall co-detection across all sites is limited for these top co-driver pairs (low Jaccard values ~0.005–0.067).
- However, conditional on the rarer substance, co-detection is often high (typically >70% and up to 100%). In other words, where the rarer partner is found, the common partner is usually present too, but the reverse is not generally true.

Queries used (you can run these to reproduce and extend)
1) Top pairs by JOINT_DRIVER_WITH frequency:
MATCH (s1:Substance)-[r:JOINT_DRIVER_WITH]-(s2:Substance)
WHERE s1.Name < s2.Name AND r.frequency IS NOT NULL
WITH s1.Name AS Substance1, s2.Name AS Substance2, max(r.frequency) AS Frequency
RETURN Substance1, Substance2, Frequency
ORDER BY Frequency DESC
LIMIT 10

2) Co-detection at the same sites for the top-frequency pairs:
MATCH (s1:Substance)-[j:JOINT_DRIVER_WITH]-(s2:Substance)
WHERE s1.DTXSID < s2.DTXSID
WITH s1, s2, j.frequency AS Frequency
ORDER BY Frequency DESC
LIMIT 10
CALL {
  WITH s1
  MATCH (s1)-[r1:MEASURED_AT]->(site1:Site)
  WHERE r1.median_concentration > 0
  RETURN count(DISTINCT site1) AS sites_sub1
}
CALL {
  WITH s2
  MATCH (s2)-[r2:MEASURED_AT]->(site2:Site)
  WHERE r2.median_concentration > 0
  RETURN count(DISTINCT site2) AS sites_sub2
}
CALL {
  WITH s1, s2
  MATCH (s1)-[r1:MEASURED_AT]->(site:Site)<-[r2:MEASURED_AT]-(s2)
  WHERE r1.median_concentration > 0 AND r2.median_concentration > 0
  RETURN count(DISTINCT site) AS sites_both
}
WITH s1, s2, Frequency, sites_sub1, sites_sub2, sites_both,
     (sites_sub1 + sites_sub2 - sites_both) AS sites_union
RETURN
  s1.Name AS Substance1,
  s2.Name AS Substance2,
  Frequency,
  sites_sub1,
  sites_sub2,
  sites_both,
  sites_union,
  CASE WHEN sites_union = 0 THEN NULL ELSE toFloat(sites_both) / toFloat(sites_union) END AS jaccard
ORDER BY Frequency DESC
LIMIT 10
